record.paper_title: Some open questions in axion theory
record.original_question: How does the axion potential induced by virtual dyonic loops change when charged fermions are present, especially in the limit where the fermions become massless and the dependence on the electromagnetic theta angle should disappear because a chiral symmetry is restored?

evidence.quote: One important open question, similar to one of the finite size effects discussed in the previous section, is: how does the axion potential induced by dyonic loops change, in the presence of charged fermions? As is familiar from the non-Abelian instanton physics, the dependence on the θγ angle should disappear in the limit when the charged fermions become massless and restore a chiral symmetry.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a U(1) gauge theory coupled to an axion field a with the standard axion–photon coupling (a/f_a) F\tilde F, and assume the existence of magnetic monopoles so that dyons (states carrying both electric charge q and magnetic charge g, with electric charge shifted by the Witten effect q = n + θ_γ/(2π) for integer n) exist in the spectrum. Virtual loops of such dyons are known to generate a nonperturbative axion potential V(a) depending on the axion field and on the electromagnetic theta angle θ_γ.

Now introduce a set of electrically charged Dirac fermions ψ_i of masses m_i, coupled minimally to the U(1) gauge field, and consider the effective axion potential V(a; θ_γ, {m_i}) induced by virtual dyonic loops in the presence of these fermions.

(a) Derive the modification of the dyon-loop-induced axion potential V(a; θ_γ, {m_i}) due to the presence of the charged fermions.

(b) Show explicitly that in the massless limit m_i → 0 for any one of the charged fermions, a chiral U(1) rotation can be used to remove θ_γ, so that the resulting axion potential is independent of θ_γ, in analogy with the disappearance of the θ-angle dependence in non-Abelian gauge theories with a massless quark.

Provide the explicit form of the potential interpolating between the heavy-fermion limit (where the known dyon-loop axion potential is recovered) and the massless-fermion limit (where θ_γ-dependence vanishes).
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicitly open problem in axion theory concerning how virtual dyonic loops generate an axion potential in the presence of charged fermions, with the expected vanishing of θ_γ dependence in the chiral limit. No subsequent work was found that computes this dyonic-loop induced axion potential with dynamical charged fermions and demonstrates the restoration of θ_γ-independence in the massless limit; the status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Some open questions in axion theory
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open questions on axion physics including the effect of charged fermions on the dyon-loop axion potential.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly identified as an open question.
